$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.
goal: The two FleetView follow-ups the payload runs carried forward and did not fix: collect_activity still reads every activity.jsonl in full on every request even in light mode, and a malformed scope_exceptions whose MEMBERS are junk renders as no block at all, indistinguishable from a run with zero exceptions.

Item A represents approximately 42% of full-request time and 35% of the light-request overhead despite being included only to derive two scalar fields.

light row requirements: serve.py:465-466 extracts _activity_last (timestamp) and _activity_n (event count) from full activity object. index.html:472,486,1627 consume these: wedged pill on list reads _activity_last; cache invalidation (rowSig()) reads both _activity_last and _activity_n; selection never fetches (index.html:257). NOT used anywhere on run list or light request path.

caching/memoization in serve.py: zero caching or memoization exists beyond ETag conditional requests on already-computed payloads. CLAUDE.md:32 states '/api/graph returns a JSON snapshot assembled from disk on every request'; CLAUDE.md:59 states 'It adds no server state: the token is recomputed from disk on every request and the client holds the only copy'. serve.py:31-33 confirms 'there is no cache to invalidate and no state held between requests'.

scope_exceptions ground truth across runs: 8 of 12 runs have the key (all as Arrays, correctly typed). Breakdown: 2 runs contain only schema docstring (450 chars starting 'ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED...'), 2 runs have empty arrays, 4 runs have real path entries. The schema docstring at _schema.json:21 correctly FAILS isRealPath() test (fails PROSE_OPENER check), so documented behavior is correct: runs with docstring-only render zero exception blocks. Python test harness does not exist: fleetview/ contains only serve.py (no test_*.py or other test files). test.js contains 193 client-side assertions (all passing, verified by running node fleetview/test.js). CLAUDE.md:284-323 describes test.js in detail; line 287 states only 'node fleetview/test.js' as test command. serve.py changes historically verified by manual reviewer testing, not automated Python tests.

items A and B are fully independent: serve.py:280 calls collect_activity() in collect_runs() (affects all requests), while index.html:534-556 isRealPath()/scopeExceptionsMalformed() are pure client rendering on already-received data. Different files, different layers, no shared code.

This is used by both build_payload() (full/light list) and build_detail() (single run detail at line 601). A detail request needs the full activity for renderActivity(); any optimization must treat the two paths differently or it will silently break detail view rendering.

BLOCKING RISK for item A: No Python test harness means any change to serve.py's hot path (collect_activity) has zero automated coverage. The measurement-based done_when approach (run a timing test command to prove the improvement) exists as a pattern, but requires human protocol amendment as stateless-server rule may conflict with certain caching approaches. Prior serves.py changes (line 89-90 in log) were merged outside this graph due to lack of automated verification.

secondary investigation: CLAUDE.md:183-191 constraint states 'FleetView depends on a data format, not a directory', using only runtime config (--fleet arg). This is load-bearing for the umbrella invariant and unrelated to items A or B.

risks: plan-killer: serve.py:280 lives inside collect_runs(), which is called for both light and full payloads. A detail request (serve.py:601) needs the complete activity data for index.html:1324-1369 renderActivity() to display the event log. Any optimization that defers or partial-reads activity.jsonl must branch the code paths or it silently breaks detail view. This is not insurmountable but requires careful design verification.

plan-killer: no Python test harness for serve.py means the change cannot be validated by automated tests. Task hints at stateless-server constraint, but the current ETag system already holds no server state; a different concern (possibly performance caching at the read level) may be the actual constraint.
Items A and B share no code or dependencies; they can be sliced independently without interaction.

plan.intent: Record item A's DEFERRAL and its revisit trigger in fleetview/CLAUDE.md, in the Architecture section beside the existing archiving paragraph (CLAUDE.md:81). This run's whole reason for re-litigating item A is that the 2026-09-04 close carried it forward and it existed nowhere on disk. Writing down the measurement AND the reason no cheap fix is also a correct one is what stops a third re-litigation. Prose only; no code changes.
plan.done_when: grep -c '17%' fleetview/CLAUDE.md -> >=1 AND grep -c '~40 runs' fleetview/CLAUDE.md -> >=1 AND grep -c '0.28%' fleetview/CLAUDE.md -> >=1 AND node fleetview/test.js -> exit 0, '193 assertions, 0 failures' (UNCHANGED: a prose slice must not move the suite) AND git -C fleetview diff --name-only master -> exactly 'CLAUDE.md'
plan.risk_reason: Prose only. No executable code, no data of any kind, no wire contract, no reader outside a human. It shares fleetview/CLAUDE.md with s2, but this is single-loop: one builder, one working tree, applied in order, so there is no fan-in for the shared file to break. A green done_when plus a scope check is sufficient evidence.

plan.intent: Item B. Make scopeExceptionsMalformed() test the field's MEMBERS as well as its type, and land the fleetview/CLAUDE.md amendment in the SAME commit. Three states, and the boundary between them is the whole slice: (1) not an Array at all -> the existing banner, exclusive, nothing else to render; (2) an Array holding any member that is not a string -> a NEW, differently-worded banner rendered ALONGSIDE whatever real paths the rest of the list held, because suppressing the paths to report the junk would hide the grants this block exists to surface -- so the control flow at index.html:1258-1276 changes from if/else-if to banner-then-block; (3) an Array of strings that all fail isRealPath -> NOT malformed, and never was: that is the schema-docstring case, it is the ordinary state of a fresh run, and it must keep rendering no block. Empty array and absent key stay silent. isRealPath's rule is untouched in both its margins. CLAUDE.md:157-162 currently documents this gap as an accepted known limitation and CLAUDE.md:310-316 lists the suite's scope_exceptions coverage; both are amended here, in the present tense, in this commit -- the 2026-09-04 lesson is that a present-tense amendment cannot be merged on its own.
plan.done_when: node fleetview/test.js -> exit 0 AND assertion count >= 199 (baseline 193) AND the new assertions cover all five boundary cases by name: [42,null] banners; [{...}] banners; a list mixing real paths with a non-string member renders BOTH the banner AND every real path; a docstring-only list renders NO banner and zero blocks; an empty list renders NO banner and zero blocks. MUTATION CHECK, run by the reviewer and required: restoring the old body -- return raw !== undefined && raw !== null && !Array.isArray(raw); -- must make node fleetview/test.js exit NON-ZERO. A suite still green under that revert is a fake test and the slice is REJECT.
plan.risk_reason: Two specific reasons, neither of them size. (1) The boundary is logic a green suite cannot fully see: a test asserting only '[42,null] shows a banner' passes identically for a wrong implementation that ALSO banners the docstring case, which would turn 2 of 8 healthy runs red on the default screen -- so the reviewer must check the negative direction and run the mutation, not just read a green line. (2) It touches fleetview/CLAUDE.md, a file s1 also touches. This block reports on the integrity of the human gate, so a wrong boundary in either direction degrades a safety signal.

architect.rationale:
SHAPE. Single-loop, and it is not close. After deferring item A there are two slices, one of them prose-only, and they share fleetview/CLAUDE.md -- fewer than 3 independent pieces and not disjoint. Even had item A proceeded, the diamond would still fail: its server change and its client contract are joined by rowSig()'s consumption of _activity_last and _activity_n, which is a real artifact edge -- exactly the ground on which 2026-09-04-payload-split declined a diamond despite disjoint files. The file test alone would have passed here, and on its own it is the wrong test.

ITEM A: DEFER, and the deferral is the finding, not a dodge. The orchestrator's numbers are accepted and not re-derived: 11.3ms of a 19.9ms light request (57%), linear in run count with a flat share, 0.28% duty cycle on a 4s poll for a local single-user read-only viewer. The architect measured the one thing left open -- what an EXACT, STATELESS design actually buys -- because 57% of a cheap thing decides nothing on its own. Over the same 12 run dirs: full collect_activity 11.240ms; an exact scan-only variant computing _activity_last and _activity_n without building agents[], events[] or tail[] costs 9.308ms, a saving of 17%; os.stat alone costs 0.290ms. The scan-only variant was checked against activity_last() on all 12 runs: 0 mismatches. So it is exactly right and exactly worth 1.9ms. The gap between 17% and 48x is not paid in engineering, it is paid in invariants, and every candidate that closes it spends one. MTIME AS THE CLOCK is dead on the orchestrator's own evidence (918s later than the last event on 2026-08-31-mobile-first-criteria, so a wedged run renders FRESHER than it is -- a false negative on the one signal this app exists to raise). A BOUNDED TAIL READ is dead because t is genuinely non-monotonic in 2026-08-26-archive-adapters and _activity_last must EQUAL what the detail pane computes -- serve.py:346-357, index.html:471-475 and a test.js assertion all say so, and breaking it makes one run read wedged in the list and healthy in the pane. FILE SIZE IN PLACE OF _activity_n is a sound append-only invalidation key but changes the WIRE CONTRACT's semantics, and both exits are bad: keep the name and the field lies to every reader; rename it and an old page's rowSig degrades to _mtime|_activity_last, which is precisely the frozen-lane bug serve.py:441-443 exists to prevent. A CROSS-REQUEST PARSE CACHE is the only design that wins big, and it is server state between requests, contradicting CLAUDE.md:32, CLAUDE.md:59 and serve.py:31-33 -- and its (size, mtime) key carries the same sub-second-write hazard the ETag section already refused, on the stated grounds that a false 304 is a live view frozen forever. So the choice today is 1.9ms for a hot-path change with zero automated coverage, or a real saving bought with an invariant. Neither is worth buying at 11ms. WIRE CONTRACT: UNCHANGED. Nothing in this plan touches serve.py, _activity_last, _activity_n or rowSig().

TRIGGER. Revisit at ~40 runs -- deliberately the SAME trigger 2026-09-04-fleetview-payload already booked for payload growth (CURRENT-STATE.md:630, 'revisit at ~40 runs or ~2 MB'), because these are the same growth curve and two triggers would be re-litigated separately. At ~40 runs a poll costs ~60ms. Revisit ARCHIVING FIRST: fleetview/CLAUDE.md:81 already names it, it costs FleetView zero code, and it is the only answer that shrinks the full payload too.

PYTHON HARNESS: unnecessary now, and building it speculatively is cost with no consumer. It IS a precondition when item A comes back, and s1 records what its first test must be so the future run inherits it: not a timing test -- a timing test cannot go red on the failure that matters, which is build_detail silently losing agents[]/tail[]/total/skipped at serve.py:601 -- but a golden-equality oracle asserting light_row's _activity_last and _activity_n equal what the full parse produces, over every run dir in a real fleet. That oracle is already known to pass at 0 mismatches on today's 12 runs.

CLAUDE.MD AMENDMENT, and it applies to item B, not item A. fleetview/CLAUDE.md:157-162 currently documents this exact gap as a deliberate known limitation ('recorded here as a known limitation rather than guarded against'), so shipping the guard makes master's prose false. It is amended INSIDE s2, not as a slice before it: the payload split's lesson is that a present-tense amendment cannot be merged alone, and code plus prose in one commit is the form that never leaves master describing behaviour the app does not have. The verbatim replacement goes to the human gate. CLAUDE.md:139-140 ('a scope_exceptions that is not a list at all renders as a stated malformed-input banner') stays TRUE and is not touched.

EDGES: no artifact edge. s2 consumes nothing s1 produces. They are ordered only because they edit the same file in the same working tree, and single-loop makes them sequential regardless -- which is why parallel_safe is false and why this is a sequence, not a diamond. Mobile-first does not apply: the registry says ui: desktop-only.
architect.edges: s1 -> s2 (ordering only, no artifact flows; they share fleetview/CLAUDE.md and the loop is sequential regardless)
not_doing: ITEM A ITSELF. No change to serve.py in this run -- not collect_activity, not collect_runs, not light_row, not build_detail. The deferral is written down (s1) instead of built.

No Python test harness. fleetview stays at one suite, node fleetview/test.js. CLAUDE.md's Testing section keeps its 'Node is needed only to run the test suite' story; only the scope_exceptions coverage sentence moves, and only in s2.

No wire-contract change. _activity_last and _activity_n keep their exact current meanings and rowSig() is not touched. If a future run wants file size as the invalidation key, that is a gate decision on its own, not a slice detail.
No mtime anywhere near the displayed clock, and no os.stat gate. Both were probed and both fail on the wedged signal.
No bounded tail read of activity.jsonl.

No caching, memoization or any state held between requests in serve.py -- and therefore NO amendment to the stateless rule at CLAUDE.md:32, CLAUDE.md:59 or serve.py:31-33. That prose stays literally true.

No change to isRealPath() or PROSE_OPENER. Both documented margins -- the over-report on a short WHY-less rationale quoting a path, and the under-report on a bare directory name or a >4-token spaced path -- stay exactly as they are and stay documented as they are.
No change to the docstring-only or empty-array renderings. 8 of 12 runs hold scope_exceptions and all 8 are correctly typed today; every one must render byte-identically after s2.
No edit to graph_agents/CURRENT-STATE.md or any other umbrella file. This run's app is fleetview; the umbrella scope rule makes that a different task.
No archiving tooling, no retention policy, no run-count cap. Named as the answer at the ~40-run trigger, not built here.
No mobile or responsive work. Registry says ui: desktop-only, so conventions/mobile-first.md does not apply.
No re-litigation of item A before the ~40-run trigger, unless a measured poll assembly exceeds 250ms sooner.

scope_exceptions: ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED, normally empty. Paths a builder may write that the approved plan does not list. guard-builder-scope.py DENIES a builder's Write/Edit outside architect.plan[].files, and this is the only way through it. Adding one is a deliberate, recorded act: pair it with deviation_from_approved_plan on the slice that needed it, and say why the gate's file set was wrong. Never add a path to silence the guard on work the human did not approve.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.
